title: Series and Sequence: Introduction to Pure Mathematics

content.text: A Sequence is an ordered set of numbers following a specific rule. A Series is the sum of the terms of a sequence. Series are classified as Finite (stops after n terms) or Infinite (continues indefinitely).

Also known as a Linear Sequence. Each term differs from the previous by a constant 'd' (common difference). The general term is Un = a + (n-1)d. The sum of the first n terms (Sn) can be found using Sn = n/2 [2a + (n-1)d] or Sn = n/2 (a + l).

Also known as an Exponential Sequence. Each term is obtained by multiplying the preceding term by a constant 'r' (common ratio). The general term is Un = ar^(n-1). Summation depends on the value of r: if r < 1, use Sn = a(1 - r^n)/(1 - r); if r > 1, use Sn = a(r^n - 1)/(r - 1).
For a GP where the common ratio |r| < 1, the terms get progressively smaller, approaching zero. The sum of all terms in such an infinite sequence is given by S∞ = a / (1 - r).
AP is used for constant growth scenarios (e.g., annual salary raises of a fixed dollar amount). GP is used for percentage-based changes (e.g., depreciation of machinery or population growth).
